body:
[A10] Owner requirement 2026-09-23 16:08: trusted local act replays must be able to run side by side. Today they are strictly serial (about 75 min each) because act 0.2.89 hard-codes the global Docker volume `act-toolcache` and names each job's workspace/env volumes from workflow and job names only (`act-<workflow>-<job>-<sha256>`), and scripts/act_ci.py turns those into an exclusive, owner-labelled boundary with a job-volume lease; it also refuses DOCKER_HOST/DOCKER_CONTEXT/DOCKER_CONFIG from the environment. Two concurrent runs of the same workflow therefore collide, and the replay is now the throughput bottleneck of the merge bar.

## Objective

N concurrent act_ci replays (N >= 2, configurable; this host has 128 threads and 53 GB RAM) of different PRs, each in its own isolation slot, with results identical to a serial run and every existing ownership, lease, interruption-cleanup and refusal guarantee preserved per slot.

## Direction (the author records the final design in a DECISION comment before dependent edits)

One dedicated Docker daemon per slot (own data-root, exec-root, socket and bridge/network range; started and owned by the runner under --sudo, or a documented systemd template), selected by an explicit --slot argument rather than by inherited environment, so the global names (`act-toolcache`, job volumes, networks) are per-daemon. Image pulls may be shared through a read-only mirror or accepted as per-slot caches; state the cost. An act fork/patch is the alternative only if daemons are shown unworkable.

## Acceptance

1. Two concurrent replays of different PRs (and of the same workflow set) complete on this host with verdicts identical to their serial runs; show a controlled collision control that fails without the isolation.
2. Per-slot guarantees: ownership labels, job-volume leases, interruption/timeout cleanup and the absence checks work per slot; a crashed or interrupted slot cannot block or corrupt another slot; leftover resources are attributable to their slot.
3. Resource bounds per slot (CPU/memory) so concurrent slots cannot starve each other or the host; documented defaults.
4. The existing single-slot behaviour and command line keep working unchanged (slot 0).
5. Offline self-tests for slot selection, refusal of inherited Docker environment, and per-slot cleanup; docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md updated.
6. No workflow semantics change (the replayed jobs are the same), no weakening of any refusal.

Manager integration (outside this PR): the serial act lock becomes a slot allocator.
title: [CI] Run trusted act replays in parallel: one isolated Docker daemon per replay slot
